cls: Substance P / neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist (prodrug of aprepitant)
quick: 150 mg IV over 20-30 min on day 1, completing ~30 min before chemotherapy
Insufficient human data; use only if clearly needed
Active moiety aprepitant excretion unknown; weigh benefit vs risk
No dose adjustment; not removed by hemodialysis
No adjustment in mild-moderate; limited data in severe (Child-Pugh >9)
Infusion-site reactions, hypersensitivity, INR if on warfarin, CYP3A4 interactions, contraceptive efficacy
summary: Fosaprepitant is an intravenous prodrug of aprepitant, a selective high-affinity substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist. Given in combination with other antiemetic agents, it is indicated in adults and children 6 months and older to prevent acute and delayed nausea and vomiting with highly emetogenic chemotherapy (including high-dose cisplatin) and delayed nausea and vomiting with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy. After IV administration it is rapidly converted (within about 30 minutes) to aprepitant, which crosses the blood-brain barrier and augments the antiemetic effect of 5-HT3 antagonists and corticosteroids. Because the active moiety is a substrate, inhibitor and inducer of CYP3A4 (and induces CYP2C9), it shares aprepitant's drug interactions, including reduced hormonal contraceptive efficacy and altered warfarin response; it is contraindicated with pimozide. Hypersensitivity and infusion-site reactions are notable IV-specific risks.
indications: Prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC), including high-dose cisplatin, in combination with other antiemetics, in adults and pediatric patients 6 months and older

Prevention of delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (MEC), in combination with other antiemetics, in adults and pediatric patients 6 months and older

dosage.n: Complete infusion approximately 30 minutes before chemotherapy; given with dexamethasone and a 5-HT3 antagonist

dosage.d: IV infusion on day 1 via central catheter per label; over 30 min (12-17 yr) or 60 min (6 mo-<12 yr)
dosage.t: Single dose (single-dose regimens) or day 1 of a 3-day regimen
dosage.n: For single/multi-day regimens, follow IV day 1 with oral aprepitant on days 2-3

dosage.d: Use with a corticosteroid and a 5-HT3 antagonist per regimen
dosage.n: Reduce co-administered oral dexamethasone dose (CYP3A4 interaction)

admin: Reconstitute/dilute per label and administer as an intravenous infusion over the specified time
Complete the infusion about 30 minutes before chemotherapy on day 1
Administer through a central venous catheter in pediatric patients
Avoid infusion into small veins; majority of infusion-site reactions occurred with vesicant chemotherapy
Use as part of a combination regimen with a 5-HT3 antagonist and a corticosteroid; reduce the dose of co-administered oral dexamethasone
moa: Fosaprepitant is a prodrug rapidly converted to aprepitant, a selective, high-affinity antagonist at human substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptors with little or no affinity for serotonin (5-HT3), dopamine or corticosteroid receptors. Aprepitant crosses the blood-brain barrier and occupies central NK1 receptors, inhibiting both the acute and delayed phases of chemotherapy-induced emesis and augmenting the antiemetic activity of 5-HT3 antagonists and corticosteroids.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to fosaprepitant, aprepitant, polysorbate 80 or any component
Concurrent use with pimozide (raised pimozide levels can cause QT prolongation)
relative: Patients relying on hormonal contraception (reduced efficacy)
Patients on warfarin or narrow-therapeutic-index CYP3A4/CYP2C9 substrates
Prior hypersensitivity to fosaprepitant/aprepitant (do not reinitiate)
monitor: Concomitant CYP3A4 substrates (e.g. some chemotherapy, midazolam, dexamethasone)

preg: There are insufficient human data on fosaprepitant or aprepitant use in pregnancy to inform a drug-associated risk; animal studies did not show clear adverse developmental effects at relevant exposures. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether aprepitant, the active moiety, is excreted in human milk; it is present in the milk of lactating rats. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding and the mother's clinical need against any potential risk to the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed for renal impairment, including end-stage renal disease; aprepitant is not removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh 5-9). There are no data in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh >9); use with caution.

major: Pimozide - contraindicated; increased pimozide levels can cause QT prolongation
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, clarithromycin) - markedly increase aprepitant exposure
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) - reduce aprepitant efficacy
CYP3A4-substrate chemotherapy and other sensitive CYP3A4 substrates - increased exposure
moderate: Oral corticosteroids (dexamethasone, methylprednisolone) - raised levels; reduce their dose
Warfarin - decreased INR (CYP2C9 induction); monitor INR for 2 weeks, particularly days 7-10
Hormonal contraceptives - reduced efficacy during and for 1 month after the last dose
Benzodiazepines metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g. midazolam, alprazolam) - increased exposure
minor: Tolbutamide and other CYP2C9 substrates - reduced exposure
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; chemotherapy-related lab changes may be seen.

serious: Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis and anaphylactic shock during or soon after infusion
Infusion-site reactions including thrombophlebitis, necrosis and vasculitis
Clinically significant drug interactions (e.g. with pimozide, chemotherapy)
rare: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis)

monitoring: Hypersensitivity reactions during and soon after infusion (discontinue and do not reinitiate if they occur)
Infusion-site reactions, particularly with vesicant chemotherapy
INR in patients on warfarin during the 2-week period (especially days 7-10) after dosing
Adequacy of contraception (back-up method during and for 1 month after dosing)
Concomitant CYP3A4/CYP2C9 substrate levels and effects; antiemetic efficacy and hydration
counsel: This is a one-time IV dose given before chemotherapy to help prevent nausea and vomiting
Tell staff immediately about flushing, rash, swelling, difficulty breathing or pain/redness at the IV site
Hormonal birth control may not work during and for 1 month after treatment - use a back-up method
If you take warfarin, you will need extra INR checks
Tell your doctor about all medicines, including over-the-counter and herbal products
pk: Converted to aprepitant within about 30 minutes of IV administration
Aprepitant exposure achieved rapidly after the infusion
Single day-1 IV dose covers acute and delayed emesis (with oral aprepitant on days 2-3 in some pediatric regimens)
Refrigerate ready-to-use injection at 2-8 C; may be kept at room temperature (20-25 C) in original carton for up to 90 days (product-specific)
pearls: Intravenous prodrug of aprepitant - converted to aprepitant within ~30 minutes, sharing its interaction profile
Use as part of a triple regimen (NK1 antagonist + 5-HT3 antagonist + corticosteroid)
Reduce co-administered oral dexamethasone dose because the active moiety inhibits CYP3A4
Watch for infusion-site reactions, especially when given near vesicant chemotherapy; avoid small veins
Pimozide is contraindicated; advise non-hormonal contraceptive back-up and extra INR monitoring with warfarin
missed: Fosaprepitant is administered by a healthcare professional as a single intravenous dose on the day of chemotherapy. There is no patient-managed missed dose; if a scheduled treatment is missed, the oncology team will determine timing relative to chemotherapy.
overdose: There is no specific information on overdose treatment for fosaprepitant or aprepitant. Drowsiness and headache occurred after a large oral aprepitant ingestion. In the event of overdose, discontinue the drug and provide general supportive care and monitoring; aprepitant is not removed by hemodialysis.
